statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-137073: in libxml2 through 2.15.4, xmlTextReaderClose() frees the reader's input buffer but leaves reader->input set, and xmlReaderNewWalker() frees it again without checking whether the reader still owns it, a double free for applications that reuse a closed reader (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-137073, https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/1212). The upstream issue is open and no upstream release carries a fix; Debian's tracker lists every release, unstable included, as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-137073). The DHI Debian libxml2 package is built from Debian's trixie source 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, which is libxml2 2.9.14 with Debian's patches. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Debian repository publishes one libxml2 build, a DHI rebuild of that Debian version, for amd64 and arm64 (libxml2, libxml2-dev, libxml2-utils and python3-libxml2, plus -dbgsym packages for libxml2, libxml2-utils and python3-libxml2); earlier DHI builds are no longer published and sort below it. The source was checked against Debian's trixie source package 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3 with Debian's patches and DHI's patches for this package applied; DHI's own patches do not touch xmlreader.c. In libxml2 2.9.14, xmlTextReaderClose frees reader->input and clears only the XML_TEXTREADER_INPUT bit in reader->allocs, and xmlReaderNewWalker calls xmlFreeParserInputBuffer on any non-NULL reader->input without checking reader->allocs, the same sequence as in the report. The vulnerable code is present in the published build, so it is affected; no fixed build has been published.
